content:
maria: Heads-up — found a reproducible case where JS sample app streaming responses merge JSON fragments when an auth refresh happens mid-stream. Python SDK doesn't exhibit this.

oliver: oof. any logs or repro steps?

maria: repro steps: start sample app (js-sdk/sample-stream), rate limit + throttle network (100ms latency), trigger token refresh by short-lived key. observed duplicate/merged fragments in client parser.

maria: logs (client-side parser output):
```
[stream] recv: "data: {\"id\":1,\"chunk\":"Hello "}

"
[stream] recv: "data: {\"id\":1,\"chunk\":"world"}

event: resume token: abc123

"
[stream] parser error: unexpected token "world\n"

```

kevin: that resume token line looks like it got appended to the second data frame, is the client splitting on double-newline reliably?

ania: sounds like the JS SDK does an abort+reconnect on auth refresh and rejoins buffers incorrectly. I recently fixed a similar bug where leftover buffer was prepended to the next chunk, causing broken JSON.

maria: interestingly the server emitted the resume token after the second chunk in the same TCP packet when throttled, so client saw: `...}

event: resume token...` appended. Python SDK handles by scanning for `

` boundaries in streaming parser, JS implementation uses a streaming decoder that can return partial lines and doesnt always flush on abort.

oliver: can you try sending Last-Event-ID on reconnect? that should avoid needing to re-send partial fragments server-side.

maria: tried that — server still resends last fragment (by design) but we end up with duplicates or merged halves if the parser doesn't drop partial buffer.

kevin: quick mitigation idea: dedupe by resume token + chunk id on client; drop fragments with id already seen.

ania: agreed as short-term. I'll open a PR to ensure the JS parser always flushes pending line fragments on stream abort and to add a simple de-dup table keyed by (resume_token, id).

maria: thanks. I've attached minimal repro commands here:
```
# start server (local)
REDWOOD_TOKEN=shortlived node server.js
# in another shell, run sample client with network throttle
node sample-stream.js --throttle 100 --force-refresh-after=1m
```

maria: also added a HAR-sized snippet of the bytes where two frames were coalesced (pasted above).

ci-bot: build #4521 started for branch fix/sse-flush-on-abort (ania) :ci:

oliver: can we add an integration test in devex/samples that simulates abort+auth-refresh under latency? this keeps regressions from sneaking in.

ania: yes, I'll add a mocha test that stubs token expiry and uses a fake net.socket to coalesce chunks. will ping when PR is up.

maria: leaving a note for docs: onboarding checklist should mention recommended `Last-Event-ID` header and that client parsers must handle partial-line flush on abort.

kevin: triage wise — mark as high for devex SDK parity. assigning to eng-ml/eng-runtime if needed.

maria: thanks everyone, will follow up with the PR link and small sample HAR. :thumbsup:
